evidence.claim: BPGD repeatedly runs BP and decimates variables until BP converges or all variables are fixed; failure to match the syndrome after full decimation is classified as non-convergence.
On the [[882,24,18<=d<=24]] B1 code under bit-flip noise, reliability-ordered decimation outperforms random decimation, and BPGD improves substantially over ordinary BP.

Reducing BP iterations per decimation round from T=100 to T=10 produces little performance degradation on the tested B1 code, while T=10 gives the best reported comparison against BP, BP-OSD order 0, and BP-SI in Figure 4.
